sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the south-western residential part of Woodbury at 50 feet to an inch. West Barber Avenue runs across the top of the sheet, with Lupton Avenue entering it at the upper right, and High and West streets cross the sheet below it, running down to the right at a slight angle. Penn Street closes the sheet along the bottom. Down the left side runs South Jackson Street, with a short length of High Street and Queen Street entering from the left margin, while Morris, Glover and Lincoln streets run north and south across the lower half and divide it into the blocks numbered 65, 66 and 67. Block 69 lies between West Barber Avenue and High Street, and block 63 between High and West streets. Almost every building is a frame dwelling, drawn in yellow with its outbuildings, set on long narrow lots; the few other buildings include a pink brick dwelling near the top, a blue concrete block garage and sheds, a small shop marked Carpenter beside West Barber Avenue, a coop, and a Builders Supplies yard near Lincoln Street. A larger building group in yellow and pink stands at the foot of the sheet beside Morris Street. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches are dashed in the streets, with hydrants and a fire alarm box marked, and street widths of 40 and 50 feet are given. A compass rose with north arrow stands at the right, and the margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 24, 25, 26, 5 and 3.
notes: West is today's W Street in OpenStreetMap; West Barber Avenue, High Street, Penn Street, Morris Street, Glover Street and Lincoln Street keep their names
Modern South Jackson Street jogs where High and West streets meet it, so no junction on Jackson Street was used for the fit
Glover Street does not reach West Barber Avenue on this sheet; the modern node where Glover and Lupton meet West Barber was left out
50 ft. SW Woodbury: W Barber, High, West (W Street), Penn; Morris, Glover, Lincoln, S Jackson. One part. S Jackson junctions left out (modern Jackson jogs).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the area south of the centre of Woodbury at 50 feet to an inch, around the point where South Broad Street, Salem Avenue and Mantua Avenue meet at Penn Street and Carpenter Street. South Broad Street comes down from the top to this meeting of streets; Salem Avenue leaves it diagonally to the lower left, lined with dwellings on narrow lots, and Mantua Avenue continues south from it to the railroad along the foot of the sheet. Penn Street runs west from the junction to Lincoln Street at the left margin, Carpenter Street runs east to Allen Street at the right, and Nelson Avenue and Railroad Avenue are the next cross streets below. Courtland Street and Allen's Lane lie in the upper right, where the north arrow is drawn. The blocks are numbered 5, 59, 62, 68, 99, 101, 106 and 107. Most buildings are frame dwellings, with a stronger commercial and light industrial group along South Broad Street and Penn Street: an auto repair shop, an auto show room, a garage, a second hand furniture store, a pool room and a modern damp wash. Two churches stand on the east side, the Bethlehem Baptist Church on Carpenter Street and the Church of God in Christ (Colored) near Railroad Avenue. Near the bottom of the sheet a building materials yard and wood shed stand beside coal bins under a wooden trestle. The railroad is lettered W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.) (Penn's Grove Branch). Water mains of 6 and 12 inches are dashed in the streets.
notes: Mantua Avenue is today's Mantua Pike (CR 649 south of Carpenter Street); the five-way junction of South Broad, Salem, Mantua and Carpenter is one node in OpenStreetMap
The railroad is the Penns Grove Secondary in OpenStreetMap
Courtland Street and South Broad Street: the modern junction lies about 11 m from the drawn one, so it was left out of the fit
Allens Lane at Carpenter Street was placed by hand, because the detector paired a lot line with the 16 foot lane
Spring Street is a short lane and does not exist today as a through street
50 ft. S of centre: S Broad / Salem / Mantua five-way, Penn, Carpenter, Nelson, Railroad Av, Allens Lane. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 lies south-east of the centre of Woodbury at 50 feet to an inch, between Carpenter Street and the Penns Grove branch of the railroad. Carpenter Street crosses the sheet from left to right. Glassboro Avenue comes down from the upper left to Carpenter Street, with East Barber Avenue branching to the right from the upper part of it and passing the end of Railroad Avenue and the tracks at the top right corner. Allen's Lane runs down the left margin and Allen Street continues the line below Carpenter Street, with Nelson Avenue crossing it, and the wide curve of a second Railroad Avenue sweeps through the lower part of the sheet beside the tracks. The sheet shows mainly frame dwellings on narrow lots along Glassboro Avenue, East Barber Avenue, Carpenter Street and Nelson Avenue. The large open tract numbered 108 holds the Carpenter Street School, a fire proof building drawn in pink and brown and marked built 1929, with the north arrow beside it. Other buildings named are the Bethel A.M.E. Church with its parish house on Carpenter Street, a club and a hall, and a tool house on the railroad. Blocks 100, 102, 104, 105, 108 and 109 are numbered. The railroad is lettered W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.) (Penn's Grove Branch), and the lines of the main railroad cross at the right edge. Water mains of 4, 6, 8 and 12 inches are shown, and widths of 16, 40 and 50 feet are given for the streets.
notes: Glassboro Avenue is today's South Barber Avenue (CR 649)
Leed's Street is today's Leeds Place
The modern Railroad Avenue is a long street through the sheet's area; only the drawn Railroad Avenue near East Barber Avenue was used
The railroad is the Penns Grove Secondary in OpenStreetMap; its crossing with Glassboro Avenue was not used because it sat 6 m off the street fit
East Barber Avenue at Railroad Avenue is detected 5 m off the fit; position is medium confidence
50 ft. SE: Glassboro Av (South Barber Av), Carpenter, Nelson, curved Railroad Av, E Barber at top right. One part; few points.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the middle of Woodbury west and south of the main crossing of Broad Street at 50 feet to an inch. South Broad Street runs down the right side of the sheet, with the business blocks of its east side at the far right, and meets West Barber and East Barber avenues at the middle of the sheet. West Centre Street and East Centre Street cross at the top, Aberdeen Place and Hopkins Street come in from the right, and High Street and West Street cross below the middle. Lupton Avenue lines the left edge, with Glover Street and Lincoln Street below it. Harrison Street and Russel Street enter at the top. The west side of South Broad Street holds the largest buildings: the Budd Motor Co. garage and repairs, a garage for sixty cars, L. A. Carey's shop, an auto body building and auto trimming shops, with long rows of concrete block sheds drawn in blue. Between Barber Avenue and West Street the blocks are rows of frame dwellings. East of South Broad Street are the Rialto Theatre, stores and apartments, the Woodbury Court Apartments, and an auto repair garage, mostly in brick. The sheet has blocks numbered 2, 3, 7, 24, 64, 68, 74, 75, 106, 107, 113, 114 and 115 around it. Hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked and water mains of 4 to 12 inches run in the streets. The compass rose stands at the left.
notes: West is today's W Street in OpenStreetMap
Russel Street (spelled with one L here) is Russell Street today; it is not drawn as a junction with West Barber Avenue, so that modern node was left out
The modern node where Glover, Lupton and West Barber meet was used at the left edge of the sheet
Harrison Street and Russell Street meet West Centre Street at the top edge of the sheet and were not detected
50 ft. Centre W/S: W Centre to West, S Broad, Lupton, Glover, Lincoln, Russel St. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the eastern side of central Woodbury at 50 feet to an inch, between East Centre Street at the top and East Barber Avenue near the foot. Railroad Avenue runs down the right side beside the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, which are drawn as a bundle of lines along the right margin together with a wooden platform and the railroad freight house. Aberdeen Place and Hopkins Street cross the sheet from left to right above the middle, with Wallace Street below them; Franklin Street runs down the middle from Hopkins Street to East Barber Avenue, and Leeds Place runs down beside Railroad Avenue. East Barber Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet from the upper left to the lower right, with Glassboro Avenue branching to the lower left and Allen's Lane running down the left edge. The blocks, numbered 107 to 116, 5, 3, 4, 8 and 22 in the margins, are almost entirely frame dwellings with some brick houses in pink, lined along the streets on narrow lots. The Central Baptist Church stands at the upper left corner, and a group of auto repair sheds and garages in blue stands in the block between Franklin Street and East Barber Avenue. A compass rose with north arrow stands near the lower left corner. Water mains of 4 to 16 inches are dashed in the streets, and street widths of 40 and 50 feet are marked.
notes: Leeds Place (St.) is today's Leeds Place
Glassboro Avenue is today's South Barber Avenue
The railroad along the right edge is the Vineland Secondary in OpenStreetMap
Control for the lower left part of the sheet is thin: Allens Lane at East Barber Avenue was not detected
50 ft. E side: E Centre to E Barber, Railroad Av, Franklin, Leeds Pl. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the civic and business centre of Woodbury at 50 feet to an inch, around the meeting of Broad Street with Delaware Street and Cooper Street. North Broad Street runs from the top of the sheet down the middle and becomes South Broad Street, labelled N. (S.) Broad, below the main crossing; West Centre and East Centre streets close the sheet along the bottom. On the east side of Broad Street stand the Woodbury Trust Co. and the Farmers and Mechanics National Bank, the 1st National Bank, the Newton Hotel, the Democrat printing office, the Constitution Co. printing building, stores, offices and a garage. Newton Avenue and E. Curtis Avenue branch off to the east. The west side holds the public buildings: the Gloucester County Court House with its clock tower and the Gloucester County Building with the jail, the Post Office, the Woodbury High School, built in 1924 and drawn in brown, the Woodbury City Hall and Public Library, the fire department building of the Friendship Fire Co. No. 1, the Kemble Memorial M. E. Church and its Sunday school, the Presbyterian Church, bowling alleys, the Atlantic Ice M'f'g Co. and an auto show room. Christ Church (Episcopal) and its chapel stand at the left. The blocks are numbered 76 to 82, 117, 118 and 119, with 9 and 10 beyond the top. Smallwood Place, Wood, Andrews, New, Harrison, Delaware, Morton and Russell streets and W. Curtis Avenue make up the west side grid. The sheet has a north arrow, and water mains of 4 to 12 inches run in the streets.
notes: East Curtis Avenue is today's Curtis Avenue
Morton Street was left out of the fit: its drawn junction with Harrison Street is about 10 m from the modern node
Delaware Street west of Broad Street continues as Cooper Street east of it; all four names meet in one node in OpenStreetMap
Wood Street and Hendrys Court run along the sheet edges and were not used
50 ft. Centre: court house, Broad, Delaware/Cooper, Newton, Curtis, Centre. One part. Morton St left out (10 m).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers a block of east-central Woodbury between Newton Avenue at the top and East Centre Street at the bottom, at 50 feet to an inch. Euclid Street runs down the right of the sheet from Newton Avenue to Cooper Street, Hendrys Court bounds the main blocks on the west, and Railroad Avenue and the West Jersey and Seashore railroad corridor close the sheet on the east, with Laurel and Green Avenue lettered along the right-hand margin. Cooper Street crosses the sheet on a slant from the left to the lower right, and East Curtis Avenue and East Centre Street run roughly parallel below it. The sheet is a mix of commercial and residential frontage. Along Cooper Street at the west end stand the Ace Motor Sales Co. garage with its showrooms, repair shop and auto parts, the offices of the Woodbury Daily Times, a monument works and the Carter Building, an office block. The Bell Telephone Company central office, a fireproof building marked as built from plans in 1929, stands at the corner of Hendrys Court and East Curtis Avenue. St. Patrick's R.C. Church occupies the block east of Euclid Street. Most of the blocks to the south are frame dwellings on narrow deep lots with outbuildings, and some apartments near the green. At the east edge the West Jersey and Seashore passenger station lies beside several tracks. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the left of the sheet. Water pipes are drawn as dashed lines with their sizes in the streets, and fire hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked. Adjoining sheets 6, 7, 10, 21 and 22 are numbered at the edges.
notes: East Curtis Avenue is today's Curtis Avenue; East Centre is East Centre Street; Euclid is Euclid Street; Cooper is Cooper Street
The railroad along the east edge is today's Vineland Secondary
Cooper Street / Hendrys Court was hand-picked: the detector paired a building edge with the street
50 ft. Cooper, Newton, E Curtis, E Centre east of Broad with the W.J.&S. station. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the northern edge of built-up Woodbury along North Broad Street, at 50 feet to an inch. Woodbury Creek crosses the top of the sheet from the right edge, where North Broad Street passes over it on a bridge, and curves down the left side, with the line between West Deptford Township and the city drawn along the creek. Most of the sheet is open, unbuilt ground between the creek and the street, divided into large lots by property lines and carrying only a few small outbuildings and one vacant dwelling near the left edge. A compass rose with a north arrow stands in the open area at the centre. The built-up frontage lies along the west side of North Broad Street at the right: a group of large vacant buildings and a filling station at the top, dwellings, the Y.M.C.A. Club House, stores, and the Paul Hotel, with garages and a few dwellings at the foot near Hunter Street. Hunter Street is drawn only at its start on the right edge, with its water pipe and a fire alarm box. Wood Street runs down the lower left, and New Street appears at the bottom beside a large block of buildings left unmapped in detail and coloured brown. Two lines of lots at the lower left are drawn from plat without buildings. Water pipes in North Broad Street and Wood Street are lettered with their sizes. The sheet carries only one street junction, North Broad Street and Hunter Street, so it is placed from that point with the scale and rotation of its neighbours. Adjoining sheets 7, 10, 11, 12 and 24 are numbered at the margins.
notes: North Broad Street is today's North Broad Street; Hunter Street is Hunter Street; Wood and New Street are Wood Street and New Street
Placed from one junction (North Broad Street and Hunter Street) with scale and rotation from the config; its only other drawn streets leave the sheet before meeting a street it shows
The creek bridge is labelled Bridge at the top right edge
50 ft. North Broad north of Hunter and Woodbury Creek. One junction only: anchored, low confidence.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the blocks of north Woodbury lying between North Broad Street on the west and the West Jersey and Seashore railroad on the east, at 50 feet to an inch. Hunter Street crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right and ends at a concrete bridge over the railroad at the right edge. Newton Avenue closes the sheet along the bottom, and Euclid Street runs the full height of the right-hand part. Above Hunter Street the large open lots hold a Society of Friends meeting house, a private hospital, sheds and a stable block; a coal yard, a hay and feed store, a blacksmith shop and a print shop stand at the top left, with a storage building. North Broad Street along the left edge carries frame dwellings and the lodge rooms, with a fire alarm box, and a private hospital stands on Hunter Street. South of Hunter Street the blocks between Broad and Euclid are dwellings on deep lots, among them several double houses along Newton Avenue; east of Euclid Street are more dwellings on regular lots. The railroad is drawn as a bundle of tracks along the right edge. A compass rose with a north arrow stands in the open land at the upper centre. The text Woodbury Creek Beyond runs along the top edge. Water pipes with sizes are lettered in the streets, and fire hydrants are marked. Adjoining sheets 7, 8, 9 and 21 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Hunter is today's Hunter Street; Euclid is Euclid Street; Newton Avenue is Newton Avenue
The railroad on the right edge is today's Vineland Secondary
North (South) Broad: the street is lettered with both names along the sheet edge
Broad Street is cut by the left edge of the sheet; the Newton Avenue junction was hand-picked on the water pipe
50 ft. Hunter, Euclid, Newton blocks beside North Broad. Four points.

sheet-11-1.description: The main part of sheet 11 shows the western edge of Woodbury around Tatum Street, at 50 feet to an inch. It runs from West Packer Street at the top to West Red Bank Avenue and down to Woodbury Creek at the bottom of the sheet, and from Cramer Avenue on the west to Mill Lane on the east. Oak Street crosses the sheet between Packer Street and Red Bank Avenue. West of Tatum Street, Red Bank Avenue is marked as not opened, and the line of Tatum Street is marked as the boundary with West Deptford Township. The area is thinly built: frame dwellings line Oak Street and Red Bank Avenue east of Tatum Street, with a row of small buildings on Cramer Avenue, and a large block in the north-west corner is marked as an athletic field with bleachers. East of Tatum Street, Mill Lane runs south towards the creek, with a few dwellings and outbuildings and a larger open lot. Woodbury Creek is drawn along the bottom right, where the scale and copyright note sit. The lower left corner of the sheet is taken up by a separate inset (part 2), set off by a heavy line, which continues the blocks west of Cramer Avenue. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths are marked.
notes: Cramer is today's Crammer Avenue
West Red Bank Avenue is today's Red Bank Avenue west of Broad Street; west of Tatum Street it is marked not opened
Mill Lane has no counterpart in OpenStreetMap

50 ft. Two parts: 1 main (W Packer to Woodbury Creek, Cramer Av to Mill Lane, Tatum St); 2 inset lower left (Frances Av to Cramer Av, Oak St to W Red Bank Av), same rotation, displaced. Cramer = Crammer Avenue.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is an inset in the lower left corner of the sheet, set off by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale and orientation as the main map. It shows the ground immediately west of Cramer Avenue: the blocks between Frances Avenue and Cramer Avenue from the unopened street north of Oak Street down to West Red Bank Avenue, with the edge of the next block west of Frances Avenue. Cramer Avenue runs along its east side, cut by the inset border. Block 282 (206) between the unopened street and Oak Street has a row of frame dwellings facing Oak Street; block 102 between Oak Street and Red Bank Avenue has a dairy with an office, cold storage and wagon sheds near Cramer Avenue, with dwellings on Red Bank Avenue. A few dwellings stand west of Frances Avenue in block 281. The unopened streets at the top and bottom of the inset are marked not opened, and the edges facing the main map are marked no exposure. A north arrow is drawn in the left margin of the inset.
notes: Cramer is today's Crammer Avenue; Frances is Frances Avenue
Inset placed from two detected junctions on Frances Avenue and two hand-picked junctions on Cramer Avenue, whose centre lies under the inset border

50 ft. Two parts: 1 main (W Packer to Woodbury Creek, Cramer Av to Mill Lane, Tatum St); 2 inset lower left (Frances Av to Cramer Av, Oak St to W Red Bank Av), same rotation, displaced. Cramer = Crammer Avenue.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the north end of Woodbury's main street, North Broad Street, and the district east of it, at 50 feet to an inch. West Packer Street crosses the top left and East Packer Street the top centre, both meeting North Broad Street where it is offset; Oak Street and West Red Bank Avenue cross it lower down on the west side. East Red Bank Avenue, labelled Cedar in parentheses, runs diagonally from the Broad Street junction to the upper right, and Green Street ends against it. North Broad Street continues down the sheet to the bridge over Woodbury Creek at the bottom, where Woodbury Creek bends across the foot of the sheet. The blocks above Red Bank Avenue are mostly dwellings, with the First Baptist Church on East Packer Street, a concrete block works at the top left, an auto service garage and a row of garages near Green Street. The Underwood private hospital, a group of connected frame and brick buildings, stands at the corner of Broad Street and West Red Bank Avenue. Below the avenue, greenhouses and a dwelling front the east side of Broad Street. Woodbury Coal and Supply Co. occupies a lot at the lower left with storage buildings and coal bins beside the creek. The right side of the sheet is largely open land between the diagonal avenue and the creek. A compass rose with a north arrow stands there, and a brown stain crosses the paper beside it. Adjoining sheets 9, 11 and 14 are numbered at the margins.
notes: West Red Bank Avenue is today's Red Bank Avenue and East Red Bank Avenue is East Red Bank Avenue; Packer streets are West Packer Street and East Packer Street
Oak is today's Oak Street; Green is Green Street
East Red Bank Avenue is also lettered Cedar on the sheet
Underwood private hospital stands at Broad Street and West Red Bank Avenue
Green Street / East Red Bank Avenue was hand-picked on the water pipe junction
50 ft. North Broad at Red Bank, Packer, Oak, with E Red Bank (Cedar) diagonal.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the north-west edge of Woodbury where it meets West Deptford Township, at 50 feet to an inch. Tatum Street runs down the middle of the sheet and carries the line between West Deptford Township on the left and the City of Woodbury on the right. Hess Avenue crosses the top, Chestnut Street crosses the sheet at two different levels on either side of Tatum Street, and Walnut Street and West Packer Street cross lower down; West Packer Street is marked Not Opened west of Tatum Street, and Walnut Street is marked Not Opened across the left. Cherry Street lies along the right edge. The left half of the sheet, in the township, is nearly all open ground divided into large lots and numbered blocks, with a few dwellings and outbuildings along Hess Avenue and Chestnut Street, and an athletic field at the lower left. East of Tatum Street are rows of frame dwellings along Hess Avenue, Chestnut Street and Cherry Street, and Public School No. 2, a brick building heated by steam, stands near the centre with a fire alarm box. Frame dwellings line the lower blocks along Walnut Street and West Packer Street. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the left. Brown stains cover the right-hand part of the sheet. Water pipes with sizes are lettered in the streets. Adjoining sheets 11, 14, 15 and 16 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Tatum is today's Tatum Street; Chestnut, Walnut and Cherry are Chestnut Street, Walnut Street and Cherry Street; West Packer is West Packer Street
Chestnut Street jogs across Tatum Street (the two sides are about 40 m apart on the ground) and is drawn as two junctions
Hess Avenue / Tatum Street was left out of the control: Hess jogs across Tatum by about 12 m and the modern node sits on neither side
Cherry Street is cut by the right edge; its junctions with Chestnut and Walnut were hand-picked from the west edge plus half the labelled width
50 ft. Tatum St (township line), Hess, Chestnut, Walnut, W Packer, Cherry. Brown stains right middle.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers a strip of north Woodbury on both sides of North Broad Street, from Hess Avenue at the top of the sheet south to Packer Street, at 50 feet to an inch. Cherry Street bounds it on the west and the railroad corridor on the east, with Green Street running parallel to Broad between them. Chestnut Street crosses west of Broad and Dare Street east of it, offset from each other, and Walnut Street crosses west of Broad near the bottom. The blocks are mainly residential, with frame dwellings set in narrow lots along Broad, Cherry and Green streets and on the cross streets. Along North Broad Street are a few larger buildings, among them Goodwill Fire Company No. 1, a garage and a lodge or hall building, and near Hess Avenue at the top a lumber yard with lumber sheds. East of Green Street, beside the tracks, is a works making cement blocks. The railroad is drawn as a bundle of several tracks along the east edge, with the sheet's north arrow beside it; the land between the tracks and Green Street is largely open. Water pipes are drawn as dashed lines in the streets with their sizes, and fire hydrants are marked. Street numbers are given along the frontages. Adjoining sheets 12, 13 and 16 are referred to at the edges.
notes: West and East Packer are today's West Packer Street and East Packer Street; Dare is Dare Street
The railroad along the east edge is today's Vineland Secondary
50 ft. Pilot. N Broad St from Hess Av to Packer St, Cherry St to the railroad (Green St, Chestnut, Dare, Walnut). Packer = East/West Packer Street.

sheet-15-1.description: The main part of sheet 15 covers the north-west edge of Woodbury, at 50 feet to an inch, on both sides of Tatum, which runs down the middle of the sheet. Crescent Avenue crosses at the top, Watkins Avenue and Dubois Avenue cross the middle, and Hess Avenue closes the sheet at the bottom. Frances runs down the left edge below Dubois Avenue. The boundary between the City of Woodbury and West Deptford is lettered along Tatum, and the blocks west of it lie in West Deptford. The ground is thinly built. East of Tatum, frame dwellings stand in regular rows on long narrow lots along Crescent Avenue, Watkins Avenue and Dubois Avenue, a few with small outbuildings, and blocks 91A, 91B, 91C and 90A are numbered. West of Tatum the lots between Watkins Avenue and Dubois Avenue carry a row of dwellings along Watkins Avenue and a few along Dubois Avenue, and blocks 202, 203 and 204 are otherwise open. Hess Avenue is drawn with a jog of about 30 feet where it meets Tatum, and Dubois Avenue and Hess Avenue are 50 and 40 feet wide. Water pipes and fire hydrants are marked in the streets, and a fire alarm box stands at Watkins Avenue. The sheet's north arrow is at the upper right. A boxed inset at the left edge, set off by a heavy line, shows blocks west of Frances and is a separate part; it is cut out of this mask.
notes: Tatum is today's Tatum Street, and Frances is Frances Avenue
Hess Avenue is drawn with a jog of about 30 feet at Tatum; the modern street is straight, and the junction was placed from the detected lines
Crescent Avenue is the top boundary of the part and only its south edge is drawn, so its junction is placed half the 50 ft width from that edge
The inset at the left edge (part 2) has no street junction and is not georeferenced
50 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Tatum, Watkins, Dubois, Hess, Crescent, Frances); 2 boxed inset at the left edge (lots west of Frances, block 272), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset at the left edge: lots west of Frances Avenue, block 272 (no street junction; needs step 6b: a carried point from a sheet that draws the same ground, or parcel corners).

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16, at 50 feet to an inch, covers the north end of Woodbury on either side of North Broad Street, which runs down the middle of the sheet, with the Pennsylvania Railroad corridor (West Jersey and Seashore) as a bundle of tracks along the east side. Crescent Avenue crosses at the top, then Watkins Avenue, Dubois Avenue and Hess Avenue at intervals down the sheet; Edith Avenue enters from the east near the top, and Washington Avenue runs beside the tracks on the right. West of Broad Street the blocks are residential, with rows of frame dwellings on long narrow lots, numbered blocks 91B, 91C and 90A, and a few dwellings marked as concrete block. The section between Dubois Avenue and Hess Avenue is mostly open. East of Broad Street are the Passenger Station and waiting room on the railroad, a gas station, a cigar factory, a freight house, and large lumber yards: Zane Lumber Co., with lumber piles and sheds, and the Woodbury Mill and Lumber Co. with a planing mill, show room and office, boiler and sawdust bin, at the bottom. The Presbyterian Cemetery occupies open ground east of Broad Street. Blocks 127, 128 and 129 are lettered on the east side. Water pipes with their sizes and hydrants are marked in the streets, and the sheet's north arrow and the Woodbury title cartouche are at the upper right. A Deptford Avenue is lettered at the top right.
notes: North Broad is today's North Broad Street
Edith Avenue is lettered (ROAD) between North Broad Street and the railroad and Edith Avenue east of Washington Avenue
The control points all lie along North Broad Street, so rotation rests on the street grid and the railroad crossing rather than on a spread of points
Washington Avenue and its junctions were not used: it runs beside the tracks and its modern line has two nodes about 40 m apart
50 ft. North Broad Street from Crescent to Hess, railroad on the east; Presbyterian Cemetery. Street points along one line.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17, at 50 feet to an inch, covers the north-west corner of Woodbury where the street plan turns from the town grid. Tatum runs down the left edge; North Broad Street, lettered Howell Avenue at the top, runs down the right edge. Hessian Avenue runs across the top as the limit of Woodbury, with West Deptford Township beyond it, Progress Avenue crosses obliquely from the lower left to the upper right, Dickerson Avenue runs across the lower middle, and Crescent Avenue closes the sheet at the bottom. Ford Avenue meets Tatum on the left. The long narrow lots between Tatum and Progress Avenue, and those between Progress Avenue and Dickerson Avenue, are drawn at an angle to the sheet. Most houses are frame dwellings; Trinity Lutheran Church stands on Progress Avenue near Tatum, a garage and several larger buildings stand on the Howell Avenue side near the top right, and a dry cleaning and dyeing works stands on Dickerson Avenue. Block 91A and block 255 are numbered. The city limits with West Deptford Township are drawn as a dash and dot line across the top and again in the middle left. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths (50, 65, 75 feet) are lettered, and the north arrow is set in the upper middle.
notes: Hessian Avenue, Progress Avenue and Dickerson Avenue are today's streets of the same name (Dickerson Street); Tatum is Tatum Street and Ford Avenue is unchanged
The street lettered Howell Avenue at the right edge is today's North Broad Street; today's Howell Boulevard lies farther north
Hessian Avenue and Crescent Avenue are boundary streets at the top and bottom of the sheet, with one side drawn, and their junctions are placed half the labelled width from the drawn edge
50 ft. NW: Tatum, Hessian, Progress, Dickerson, Crescent, North Broad (printed Howell Av.).

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18, at 50 feet to an inch, shows the Colonial Manor subdivision in West Deptford Township, north-west of Woodbury, laid out in square blocks from a plat. Colonial Avenue runs along the top, Elberne Avenue crosses the middle, and Hessian Avenue along the bottom marks the boundary with the City of Woodbury, with the township line drawn along it. Tatum runs down the left edge, McKinley Avenue runs down the centre, and Howell Avenue runs obliquely down the right side beside the railroad, a bundle of tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad crossing the right third of the sheet. Broadway is lettered at the far right. The blocks are cut into narrow numbered lots, with the lot letters P, Q and R on the larger tracts, but only a scatter of houses stands on them: frame dwellings near Tatum and McKinley Avenue, the Colonial Manor Methodist Episcopal Church on Tatum at Elberne Avenue, and a few dwellings and sheds along Howell Avenue. The subdivision is named Colonial Manor in the upper right, near the sheet title cartouche, and the north arrow is at the right. Streets are 50 feet wide, Howell Avenue 50 feet, and Broadway 66 and 80 feet. Taft Avenue is lettered at the left edge, beside sheet 19.
notes: Tatum Avenue and Tatum Street are both today's Tatum Street; Taft Avenue, McKinley Avenue, Elberne Avenue, Hessian Avenue, Colonial Avenue and Broadway keep their names
Howell Avenue appears to be today's North Broad Street: the Elberne Avenue junction there was placed with the others and fitted to within 2.4 m

A hand-picked point at Colonial Avenue and McKinley Avenue, on the top boundary street, fitted about 7 m from the other points and was left out; the subdivision is drawn square from a plat and the modern Colonial Avenue line may not agree with it
Only five junctions were used, all in the lower two thirds of the sheet; the top is held by the fit alone
50 ft. Colonial Manor east part (Tatum, Taft, McKinley, Elberne, Hessian, Broadway); fitted rotation -41 deg, 5 points.

sheet-19-1.description: The main part of sheet 19 shows Colonial Manor, a suburban development in West Deptford Township north-west of Woodbury, at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is drawn turned, with north towards the upper left. Avenues named for presidents and early settlers run up the sheet: Cleveland, Puritan, Pilgrim, Washington, Lafayette and Lincoln avenues, with Tatum and Taft avenues on the east. They are crossed by Wilson Avenue at the top, Colonial Avenue across the middle, Elberne Avenue and Hessian Avenue near the bottom, where the West Deptford Township line follows Hessian Avenue. Howell Avenue and the railroad cross the upper right corner, and McKinley Avenue joins Colonial Avenue on the east. The blocks are lettered A to S and divided into many narrow numbered building lots, most of them still empty; frame dwellings are scattered along the avenues, more densely towards Lincoln and Tatum avenues. The Colonial Manor Public School stands near Hessian Avenue between Lafayette and Lincoln avenues, a water tank stands at Tatum and Elberne avenues, and a fire house is drawn on Colonial Avenue near Lincoln Avenue. The name Colonial Manor is spelled out in large letters across the lots. The lower left corner holds an inset (part 2) set off by a heavy line.
notes: Tatum Avenue is today's Tatum Street; Howell Avenue is Howell Boulevard; Cleveland Avenue has no counterpart under that name in OpenStreetMap
Junctions on Colonial Avenue were not detected (offset crossings); residuals of 2 to 7 m across the part suggest the development is drawn from its plat rather than surveyed

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main, Colonial Manor (Wilson, Colonial, Elberne, Hessian Avs x Puritan to Lincoln, Tatum, Taft), turned about -65 deg; 2 inset lower left (Tatum St, Ford and Progress Avs south of Hessian Av), same rotation, displaced. Colonial Manor drawn from plat: residuals 2-7 m.

sheet-19-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 19 is an inset in the lower left corner of the sheet, set off by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale (100 feet to an inch) and orientation as the main map, with its own north arrow pointing to the upper left. It shows the ground south of Hessian Avenue along Tatum Street: the corner of Taft Avenue and Hessian Avenue at its top, and the blocks along Ford Avenue and Progress Avenue between Tatum Street and the West Deptford Township line, which crosses the lower left of the inset. Block 254 (201) between Ford and Progress avenues and the lots north of Ford Avenue are built up with rows of frame dwellings, more closely than the Colonial Manor lots of the main map. A fire alarm box and hydrants are marked at Tatum Street and Progress Avenue. The ground beyond the inset's edge towards sheet 17 is marked vacant beyond.
notes: Tatum Avenue and Tatum Street are both printed for the same street, today's Tatum Street

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main, Colonial Manor (Wilson, Colonial, Elberne, Hessian Avs x Puritan to Lincoln, Tatum, Taft), turned about -65 deg; 2 inset lower left (Tatum St, Ford and Progress Avs south of Hessian Av), same rotation, displaced. Colonial Manor drawn from plat: residuals 2-7 m.

sheet-20-1.description: The main part of sheet 20 shows the Woodbury Park district north-east of the city centre and the adjoining part of Deptford Township, at 100 feet to an inch. On the west it is bounded by Howell Avenue, the West Jersey and Seashore railroad and North Broad Street; Broadway runs diagonally up the left side. Pine, Spruce and Clinton streets cross the subdivision of Woodbury Park, whose name is lettered across its lots, with Grand and Sumner streets and Fisher Avenue below them. Park Avenue crosses the sheet near the middle and carries the boundary between Deptford Township and the City of Woodbury. South of it are North Evergreen (Cleveland) Avenue, Washington Avenue, Lippincott Street, Deptford Avenue and Edith Avenue, with unopened Roosevelt, Taft and Wilson avenues at the bottom right. Most lots hold frame dwellings. Named buildings include the A.M.E. Church on Park Avenue, the Helping Hand Fire Company, the Woodbury German Singing Society club house, the Park Avenue Public School and the cement block factory of E. P. Henry and Sons on Lippincott Street. Two insets are set off by heavy lines: Broadway north of Pine Street in the upper right (part 2) and the blocks south of Edith Avenue in the lower middle (part 3).
notes: Renamed since: Pine is Peach Street, Spruce is Magnolia Street, Sumner is Summer Avenue, Grand is Grace Avenue, North Evergreen (Cleveland) is North Evergreen Avenue
Grace Avenue was left out of the control: its modern junctions sat 5 to 9 m from the drawn Grand Street
Acton Place has no counterpart in OpenStreetMap

100 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Woodbury Park, Broadway to Lippincott St, Pine to Edith Av); 2 upper right (Broadway from Pine St to Gilbert Av); 3 inset lower middle (Washington and N Evergreen Avs south of Edith Av). Renamed: Pine = Peach St, Spruce = Magnolia St, Sumner = Summer Av, Grand = Grace Av (left out, displaced), N Evergreen (Cleveland) = North Evergreen Av, Station Av = Station Drive.

sheet-20-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 20 occupies the upper right corner of the sheet, set off from the main map by a heavy line, at 100 feet to an inch. It shows Broadway north of Pine Street up to Gilbert Avenue, east of the railroad, which is noted beyond the heavy line on the west. Colonial Avenue meets Broadway from the west near the middle of the part, and Pine Street runs along the heavy line at its foot. The lots along both sides of Broadway hold frame dwellings and many small outbuildings, several of them marked as coops; a garage with a store stands on the east side of Broadway near Gilbert Avenue, and a blacksmith shop behind it. The land east of the Broadway lots, in block 146, is largely open. A large compass rose stands below the part, and the sheet's title cartouche sits at its top.
notes: Pine Street is today's Peach Street
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Broadway and Gilbert Avenue) with the scale of the main part and a rotation fitted by eye to the modern parcels; low confidence

100 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Woodbury Park, Broadway to Lippincott St, Pine to Edith Av); 2 upper right (Broadway from Pine St to Gilbert Av); 3 inset lower middle (Washington and N Evergreen Avs south of Edith Av). Renamed: Pine = Peach St, Spruce = Magnolia St, Sumner = Summer Av, Grand = Grace Av (left out, displaced), N Evergreen (Cleveland) = North Evergreen Av, Station Av = Station Drive.

sheet-20-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 20 is an inset in the lower middle of the sheet, set off by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows the narrow strip south of Edith Avenue between the West Jersey and Seashore railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) on the west and North Evergreen Avenue on the east. Washington Avenue leaves Edith Avenue in a curve and runs south to Station Avenue, where it turns and continues south past a row of frame dwellings in block 265. Block 264 (151) between Edith Avenue, Washington Avenue and Station Avenue is laid out in lots with several frame dwellings, and block 151 east of Washington Avenue has a few more. The edges of the inset facing the main map are marked no exposure, and its southern edge vacant beyond.
notes: Station Avenue is probably today's Station Drive; the modern Washington Avenue and Station Drive do not follow the drawn lines closely
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Edith Avenue and North Evergreen Avenue) with the atlas scale and the inset's own north arrow; low confidence

100 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Woodbury Park, Broadway to Lippincott St, Pine to Edith Av); 2 upper right (Broadway from Pine St to Gilbert Av); 3 inset lower middle (Washington and N Evergreen Avs south of Edith Av). Renamed: Pine = Peach St, Spruce = Magnolia St, Sumner = Summer Av, Grand = Grace Av (left out, displaced), N Evergreen (Cleveland) = North Evergreen Av, Station Av = Station Drive.

sheet-21-1.description: The main part of sheet 21 covers the south-eastern part of Woodbury between Hunter Street and Cooper Street, at 100 feet to an inch. On the west, Laurel Street, Maple Avenue and Holyroyd Place form a closely built residential district of frame and brick dwellings north and south of Hunter Street. Hester's Branch runs down the middle of the sheet in a broad open valley, with a tributary from the creek at the top left. East of it, North Woodland Avenue, North Evergreen Avenue and North Bayard Avenue run south from Hunter Street to Cooper Street, crossed by Spruce Lane; their blocks are only partly built up, with frame dwellings, the Evergreen Hall Apartments near North Bayard Avenue and Cooper Street, and open lots. Cooper Street runs along the bottom of the sheet. The upper right quarter of the sheet is a separate part (part 2), set off by a heavy line, showing the ground east of North Bayard Avenue around the Woodbury Country Club. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in the streets, and adjoining sheets 8, 10 and 22 are referred to at the edges.
notes: Holyroyd Place is today's Holroyd Place; Hunter is Hunter Street

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Hunter St to Cooper St, Laurel St to N Bayard Av, Hester's Branch); 2 upper right (N Bayard Av to Hunter St, Spruce Lane to Cooper St, Woodbury Country Club), displaced. Holyroyd Pl = Holroyd Place.

sheet-21-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 21 fills the upper right quarter of the sheet, set off from the main map by a heavy line, at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows the ground east of North Bayard Avenue between Spruce Lane and Cooper Street, with Rugby Place and East Rugby Place curving through it to Hunter Street on the east. North of Cooper Street the lots along North Bayard Avenue, Spruce Lane and Rugby Place hold a few frame dwellings and garages. South of Cooper Street, the block east of South Bayard Avenue is taken up by the Woodbury Country Club, with its club house, and a few dwellings on Woodside Place at the bottom left. A short stretch of creek is drawn along the west edge of the part. The heavy line at the bottom is marked no exposure, and the sheet's title cartouche sits at the top right.
notes: Hunter is today's Hunter Street

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Hunter St to Cooper St, Laurel St to N Bayard Av, Hester's Branch); 2 upper right (N Bayard Av to Hunter St, Spruce Lane to Cooper St, Woodbury Country Club), displaced. Holyroyd Pl = Holroyd Place.

sheet-22-1.description: Sheet 22 covers the south-eastern edge of Woodbury from Cooper Street south to Carpenter Street and the new streets beyond East Barber Avenue, at 100 feet to an inch. Along the west side Green Avenue follows the West Jersey and Seashore railroad, with Laurel Street, Maple Avenue and Hopkins Street at the top left. Two large works stand there: the patent medicine works of G. G. Green, with a pond and green house in its grounds, and the factory of the Belber Trunk and Bag Company. Hester's Branch creek winds down the middle, with Lake Drive beside it. East of the creek, North and South Woodland Avenue and North and South Evergreen Avenue run south from Cooper Street, with Woodside Place, South Bayard Avenue and the City Park on the east; beyond Bayard Avenue are the golf links of the Woodbury Country Club. East Barber Avenue sweeps across the sheet from Green Avenue to the south-east corner, with Maple Avenue and Burholme Avenue south of it and Hemlock Terrace and Griscom Drive, laid out with few houses, in the lower right. The lower middle holds a small inset (part 2) of the tracks at Carpenter Street.
notes: Burholme Avenue and East Barber Avenue keep their names today
The inset of the tracks at Carpenter Street (part 2) was not placed

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Cooper St to Carpenter St, Green Av to S Bayard Av; G. G. Green works, Belber Trunk & Bag Co.); 2 small inset lower middle (tracks at Carpenter St and Green Av, Glassboro Av), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: railroad tracks at Carpenter Street and Green Avenue, Glassboro Avenue (block 134) (Carpenter Street no longer crosses the tracks and the only surviving junction (Carpenter / Railroad / South Barber) lies outside the inset; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-4 (Carpenter Street and the tracks)).

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the south-east part of Woodbury between Woodbury Creek, drawn across the top, and Myrtle Avenue, which curves across the bottom. Streets run in a regular grid: North and South Warren, Drexel, Childs, Girard, American, Columbia and Horace run down the sheet, and Harding Avenue, Grant, Delaware and West Centre cross them. Delaware is the main cross street, with the blocks above it in the northern streets and those below in the southern. Most blocks are densely divided into narrow lots and carry small frame dwellings in rows, particularly between Girard and Horace and between Harding Avenue and Delaware. The west side, between Warren and Childs, is thinly built and the area north of Grant is mostly open, with a few outbuildings. The City of Woodbury limit with West Deptford Township is drawn down the left edge, and Delaware and the blocks beyond are partly cut by it. Numbered blocks 9 to 14, 23 to 31 and 285 to 289 are lettered. Water pipes, hydrants and widths of 50 feet are marked in the streets. The sheet's north arrow is at the upper left and the Woodbury title cartouche at the upper right. Adjoining sheets 24, 25 and 14 are named in the margins.
notes: Grant is today's Grant Avenue; Harding Avenue is Harding Street; Delaware is Delaware Street; West Centre is West Centre Street; the numbered N. and S. streets are North and South Warren, Drexel, Childs, Girard, American, Columbia and Horace Street; South Warren is South Warren Avenue
North Horace is drawn about 11 m west of South Horace at Delaware; the modern streets are offset by about 4 m, and only the South Horace junction was used
Myrtle Avenue is a curved street and was not used for control
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; fitted scale 3.97 px/ft
100 ft. West Woodbury: Warren to Horace, Harding to Myrtle.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the western part of Woodbury along Woodbury Creek, at 100 feet to an inch. Woodbury Creek crosses the top of the sheet, curving from the upper left to the upper right, and the boundary between West Deptford Township and the City of Woodbury is drawn along it. Delaware Street runs across the middle of the sheet from left to right and West Centre Street and Myrtle Avenue run parallel below it, crossed by the north-south streets Horace, Warner, Davis and Jackson, each lettered North above Delaware Street and South below it. West Barber Avenue crosses the bottom, with Spring Street and Lupton Avenue running down the right half, and Wood Street and Harrison are lettered at the right edge. Briar Hill Lane curves through the upper left. The blocks are almost all frame dwellings on regular lots, mostly detached houses with a few stores and garages, with larger vacant and open ground between Delaware Street and the creek and in the middle blocks near Jackson Street. A small group of buildings stands on the creek at the upper right where Wood Street meets it, and a compass rose with a north arrow stands in the open area above. Water pipes with sizes are lettered in all the streets, and fire alarm boxes are marked. Adjoining sheets 2, 5, 7, 9, 23 and 25 are numbered at the margins.
notes: West Centre is today's West Centre Street and Delaware is Delaware Street; Lupton Avenue, Spring, Wood and Harrison are Lupton Avenue, Spring Street, Wood Street and Harrison Street
Myrtle Avenue is lettered (Stratton) beside it
Briar Hill Lane is today's Briarhill Lane in the street data; it was left out of the control because its modern line does not follow the drawn curve
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch (printed scale)
100 ft. West Woodbury: Delaware, W Centre, Myrtle, W Barber from Horace to Lupton.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the south part of Woodbury, from Myrtle Avenue at the top to the West Jersey and Seashore Penns Grove Branch of the Pennsylvania Railroad and Logan and Emerson at the bottom. The same regular grid as sheet 23 continues: South Girard, Columbia, Horace, Warner, Davis and Jackson run down the sheet, crossed by High, King, Queen and Prince. The densest building is in the strip along Myrtle Avenue at the top and on the blocks east of Warner, where dwellings stand on narrow lots; the Stratton section is lettered on the north-east side. Most blocks south of High are large and nearly empty, with numbered blocks 15 to 22, 34 to 40, 43 and 252, a few dwellings on King and Queen, and the H. Wagner premises, a house with a hen house, on a private lane drawn obliquely near the right edge. The railroad crosses the lower part as a pair of tracks, with the city limits against West Deptford Township drawn along it and then turning south; narrow lots with dwellings line the railroad on Logan at the bottom right. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 50 feet are marked. The north arrow is at the upper left, and a Woodbury title cartouche is at the upper right. Adjoining sheets 23, 24 and 26 are named in the margins.
notes: High, King, Queen and Prince are today's High Street, King Street, Queen Street and Prince Street; the numbered S. streets are South Girard, Columbia, Horace, Warner, Davis and Jackson Street
Myrtle Avenue is a curved street and was not used for control; Logan and Emerson lie by the railroad and were not used
West Barber Avenue at the right edge is probably today's Barber Avenue
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; fitted scale 3.97 px/ft
100 ft. High to Prince, Girard to Jackson, Penns Grove branch at the bottom (Stratton).

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the west end of Woodbury at 100 feet to an inch, with the sheet turned about 15 degrees from north. The built-up part is in the upper right, where Penn, Glover, Lincoln, Morris and Logan streets enclose small rectangular blocks of frame dwellings on narrow lots. Among them are the West End Public School, St. John's Evangelical Lutheran Church, the Cascade Laundry with its hose house and a steam, light and power building, and C. J. Sanderson's hot houses (greenhouses) on block 56. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), Pennsgrove Branch, crosses the middle of the sheet in a broad band of tracks, with West End Station beside Morris Street. South of the tracks Salem Avenue runs diagonally from the upper right to the lower left. Leona Avenue and two stretches of Everett Avenue leave it at an angle, and the blocks beside them hold dwellings and outbuildings, with a larger works at the left edge near the city limit. Emerson Street crosses the upper left of this area. The lower left and lower centre are mostly open land with a few scattered houses. A dash-dot line labelled City of Woodbury and West Deptford Township crosses the lower part of the sheet. Mantua Avenue runs down the right edge, with H. Linsk & Co., a maker of wearing apparel, and the Hall of the I.B.P.O.E. of Woodbury on its west side and the cross streets of sheet 27 meeting it from the east. The compass rose and a scale bar for 100 feet to an inch are at the left and bottom. Adjoining sheets 25, 27, 32, 33, 52, 53, 55, 56 and 60 are cited on the margins.
notes: Salem Avenue and Leona Avenue keep their names; Mantua Avenue is today's Mantua Pike; Penn, Logan, Morris, Glover, Lincoln, Emerson and South Jackson are today's Penn Street, Logan Street, Morris Street, Glover Street, Lincoln Street, Emerson Street and South Jackson Street
Everett Avenue is not in the current OpenStreetMap street data and was not used for control
The railroad labelled W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.) Pennsgrove Branch is today's Penns Grove Secondary
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the fitted scale agrees (about 4.0 pixels per foot)
100 ft. West End: Penn, Glover, Lincoln, Morris, Logan; Salem and Leona Avs; Penns Grove branch.

sheet-27-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 27 is the area west of the heavy line that divides the sheet, in West Deptford Township just beyond the Woodbury city limit, at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 25 degrees from north. Mantua Avenue runs down the left side. Off it to the east run Bellevue, Packard and Stuart avenues, with Lafayette Avenue as the main cross street and Naomi Avenue and Acton Court lower down; two further streets east of Lafayette are lettered Not Named. The blocks are narrow lots with frame dwellings, and the lots near Naomi Avenue carry a close row of small dwellings, some coloured pink for brick. Institutions marked are the Mt. Zion M.E. Church on Stuart Avenue and a Church of God (colored) near the Not Named streets. At the top the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, Penns Grove Branch, and Railroad Avenue cross the sheet, and a railroad storage yard lies at the upper right. A wide corridor of the West Jersey and Seashore main line (Cape May Division) curves across the middle from the lower left to the heavy line, with South Evergreen Avenue beside it. Lower on the sheet are an auto wrecking yard, coal bins and a wooden trestle, and the filling station and tanks of the Standard Oil Company of New Jersey. The dash-dot line marked City Limits and Boro Limits, with the label Boro of Woodbury Heights, crosses the sheet east to west, and the West Deptford Township boundary runs down beside Mantua Avenue. The compass rose and the scale bar are at the left.
notes: Mantua Avenue is today's Mantua Pike, Stuart Avenue is Stuart Street and the Penns Grove Branch is the Penns Grove Secondary
Acton Court is marked Arbitrary (a proposed street); by spacing from Naomi Avenue and Stuart Avenue it matches today's Reid Street, which is the control point used, but this is an inference
Bellevue Avenue was left out of the control because its modern junction with Lafayette Avenue lay 20 m from the drawn one
The part is cut from part 2 of the sheet along the heavy double line

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 Mantua Avenue district (Lafayette, Naomi, Stuart, Packard, Acton Ct = Reid St?), Bellevue left out (20 m); 2 Woodbury Heights strip (Maple, Mercer, Glassboro Av), anchored on Maple/Mercer, low confidence.

sheet-27-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 27 is the strip east of the heavy line, in the Borough of Woodbury Heights, at 100 feet to an inch. Its own north arrow points slightly east of straight up. Glassboro Avenue runs down the right side and is marked with the borough line between Woodbury Heights and Deptford Township; a 'No Exposure' note lies beyond it. Lots on its west side carry frame dwellings and sheds in a regular row of numbered lots (block 38), with block 304 at the upper right and block 303 beside it. In the centre is a broad corridor holding West Jersey Avenue, lettered as 100 feet wide, and the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, Cape May Division, with Barlow Avenue beside it. Mercer Street leaves Maple Avenue northward as the boundary of block 38, and Maple Avenue crosses the bottom of the part. A railroad spur curves into the lower left. The heavy double line forming the left edge is lettered Vacant Beyond. The rest of the part is mostly open land, with a few dwellings and outbuildings near West Jersey Avenue.
notes: Glassboro Avenue is today's Woodbury-Glassboro Road and Mercer is Mercer Street
Only one street junction, Maple Avenue and Mercer Street, was usable, so the part is placed on that point with the scale taken from neighbouring sheets: low confidence
West Jersey Avenue and Barlow Avenue as drawn do not fit the spacing of the modern streets of the same names and were not used

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 Mantua Avenue district (Lafayette, Naomi, Stuart, Packard, Acton Ct = Reid St?), Bellevue left out (20 m); 2 Woodbury Heights strip (Maple, Mercer, Glassboro Av), anchored on Maple/Mercer, low confidence.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows the western part of the Woodbury Heights plan at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 90 degrees so that north lies to the left; its compass rose at the upper left points that way. The map is a regular grid of long narrow blocks. West Jersey Avenue runs along the top, with Fourth, Third and Second streets crossing the sheet below it, and Holly, Cherry, Maple, Poplar and Elm avenues run down the page between them. The blocks are numbered 4 and 5 and 10 to 13 at the bottom, 23 to 26 in the middle and 27 to 30 at the top. Almost all of the plan is subdivided lots, drawn as long ruled strips with no buildings. Dwellings stand only in the top row of blocks, along West Jersey Avenue, and in the blocks beside Poplar and Elm avenues, where a church (lettered Woodbury Heights 1st Presbyn Church) and a fire department building stand near Poplar Avenue. A few six-inch water mains are drawn in the streets. At the left a long vertical line forms the edge of the plan and the area beyond it is blank, with block 6 marked. At the bottom right Elm Avenue turns into a road marked Not Named. The sheet's right-hand strip, marked 29, continues on sheet 29. Street widths of 50 and 60 feet are noted along the sides.
notes: The sheet is turned so that north lies to the left; the fitted rotation is about -87 degrees

West Jersey Avenue, 2nd Street, 3rd Street and 4th Street are today's West Jersey Avenue, 2nd Street (North 2nd Street at the top), 3rd Street and 4th Street; Holly, Cherry, Maple, Poplar and Elm avenues keep their names
Most of the plan was unbuilt in 1929, so the control points come from street junctions on the modern grid
100 ft. Woodbury Heights grid (West Jersey Av, 2nd-4th Sts, Holly to Elm), turned (north to the left).

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 continues the Woodbury Heights plan eastward from sheet 28 at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 90 degrees so that north lies to the left. West Jersey Avenue runs along the top, with Fourth, Third and Second streets across the sheet below it, and Elm, Central, Oak, Linden and Beech avenues run down the page between them. Willow Avenue is the right-hand street and is also the borough line between Woodbury Heights and Deptford Township. The blocks, numbered 14 to 22 and 31 to 35, are laid out as long ruled strips of lots, almost all vacant. Dwellings are concentrated in the top row of blocks along West Jersey Avenue and in the block between Elm and Central avenues, near Fourth Street, where a larger brick building and a pair of smaller ones stand. Six-inch water mains are drawn along several of the streets and house numbers are given along the lots. Southwest of the grid a wedge of land beside Elm Avenue is cut by a street marked Not Named, with a few dwellings at the lower left. The compass rose stands at the right edge beside Willow Avenue, and the scale bar and stamp are at the lower right. Adjoining sheets 28 and 30 are cited at the margins.
notes: The sheet is turned so that north lies to the left; the fitted rotation is about -87 degrees
Willow Avenue is lettered Woodbury Heights Boro Limits and Deptford Township and is not in the current street data; it was not used for control
West Jersey Avenue, 2nd, 3rd and 4th streets and Elm, Central, Oak, Linden and Beech avenues are today's streets of the same names
Most of the plan was unbuilt in 1929, so the control points come from street junctions on the modern grid
100 ft. Woodbury Heights grid (Elm to Willow), turned (north to the left).

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 shows the centre of Woodbury Heights at 100 feet to an inch, turned a few degrees clockwise from north. Glassboro Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, and the cross streets are Maple Avenue at the top and Elm, Candunas, Asme, Helen, Lake, Clement and Park avenues below it. Academy Avenue runs parallel to Glassboro on the west, enclosing large blocks. At the left edge the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, Cape May Division, run beside West Jersey Avenue, with the Woodbury Heights Station and a storage shed beside them. On the large block 310 stand the Woodbury Hgts School, built in 1924, with brick walls and fire extinguishers noted, and the Woodbury Hghts Fire Co.; next to them are the sub-station of the Peoples Gas Co. of Glassboro, N.J. and, at the top of the sheet in block 308, two greenhouses with a boiler house. St. Peters Church (Episcopal) stands on Lake Avenue in block 320. Most of the houses are frame dwellings with coops and sheds on long narrow lots along Glassboro, Candunas, Lake and Park avenues, and an auto wrecking yard is on Glassboro Avenue near Asme Avenue. A dash-dot line from the top centre to the right edge, lettered Boro Limits, separates Woodbury Heights from Deptford Township. The compass rose is near the top, and the scale bar and library stamp are at the bottom. Sheet 31 is cited at the right and the sheets numbered 27, 28 and 29 on the left.
notes: Glassboro Avenue is today's Woodbury-Glassboro Road; Asme Avenue and Candunas Avenue are today's Asam Avenue and Candidus Avenue, matched by position
The Cape May Division line beside West Jersey Avenue is today's Vineland Secondary
The fitted scale (about 3.94 pixels per foot) agrees with the 100 feet to an inch printed on the sheet
100 ft. Woodbury Heights centre: Glassboro and Academy Avs, Maple to Park.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the southern part of Woodbury Heights around Glen Lake at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 10 degrees clockwise from north. Glen Lake fills the middle of the sheet, a narrow lake with a heavy outline that runs from the top centre down to the right of the sheet. West of the lake, Lake Avenue follows the shore in two curved stretches, with Park Avenue and Walnut Avenue entering from the west and Woodside, West Spring and South Spring avenues radiating out of its southern end. Crestmont Avenue runs down the left side beside the City of Woodbury Reservoir, drawn with its walls and a capacity of 14 million gallons. Walnut Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, with long narrow lots on both sides, and Glenwood Avenue runs down the east side of the lake and curves towards Sunside Avenue and Chestnut Avenue, which closes the bottom of the sheet. East of Glenwood Avenue are long ruled lots with chicken coops and sheds, numbered 55. A heavy dashed line along the right edge is lettered Woodbury Heights Boro Limits and Deptford Township, with Borough Line Road beside it. Most houses are frame dwellings with outbuildings and coops, and there are a few buildings beside Walnut Avenue near the lake. The compass rose is in the centre, and the scale bar and library stamp are at the bottom right. Blocks 45 to 55 and 315 are numbered.
notes: Placed from only four junctions on Spring, Sunside, Walnut, Glenwood and Chestnut avenues; the Lake Avenue streets and Crestmont Avenue lie 8 to 20 m from the drawn lines and were left out of the control
Boundary Road in today's street data lies about 4 to 15 m from the drawn Borough Line Road and was left out of the control
Walnut Avenue, Lake Avenue, Park Avenue, Spring Avenue, Crestmont Avenue, Chestnut Avenue, Sunside Avenue and Glenwood Avenue are today's streets of the same names
The fitted rotation (about 11.6 degrees) is 3 degrees from the compass rose drawn on the sheet
100 ft. Woodbury Heights south: Glen Lake, Walnut, Glenwood, Chestnut, Spring. Four points; Boundary Rd, Lake Av, Crestmont, Park left out (7-20 m).
